html:
SMTO-FIL-0022 — The computer didn't let SMTO use this file

GUID: 55123110-c050-4915-8b6d-a92ff0857b4b
Slug: file-permission-denied
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The account the Gateway runs as on that computer isn't allowed to open or change this file, or the file is read-only. SMTO's own permission settings can't override the computer's file permissions.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway's computer, open the file's properties and check that it isn't marked read-only and isn't on a read-only or locked drive. A read-only file or drive blocks changes no matter who asks.
  2. Ask the person who manages that computer to give the account the Gateway runs as access to just this file or folder, not the whole drive. The computer, not SMTO, decides who may open the file, and narrow access keeps other files safe.
  3. Or ask SMTO to save the result in a folder it already writes to, such as its working folder. A destination the Gateway's account can already use avoids the blocked location.
  4. If SMTO was changing several files, check which ones already changed before asking it to repeat the step. The block may have hit partway through, after some files were already updated.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens or saves the file and the step completes.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer. Don't turn off SMTO's safety or permission settings to fix this; they can't change the computer's file permissions.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation was denied by the operating system (EACCES/EPERM, Windows access-denied or privilege codes) or targeted a read-only destination under the Gateway's OS account.

What this means

  • The file operation encountered an operating-system access restriction or a read-only destination. The Gateway’s actual OS account and destination permissions matter; application approval cannot grant access the operating system denies. Earlier file changes remain governed by their receipts.

Why this can happen

  • The OS reports access or privilege denial, or the destination is read-only.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the actual Gateway OS account and the exact traversal, read or write permission required for this path. Distinguish a read-only destination from account permissions before changing either.

How to fix it

  • Identify the Gateway process's OS user and check traversal, read and write permissions and the read-only attribute on the path in path_context. Grant only the specific access needed, or choose a destination that account can write; SMTO unsafe-action or permission policy cannot grant filesystem access (gateway_core/file_common.error_kind, Stage).
  • Repair OS/filesystem permissions or use an identity or destination with access. SMTO unsafe-action policy does not grant filesystem access.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Confirm the actual Gateway OS identity has the exact required traversal/read/write access on this path.

What not to do

  • Do not disable SMTO policy guards to repair OS permissions.
  • Do not grant broad recursive permissions as a default fix.

Technical notes

  • Filesystem errno/winerror or a read-only destination rejects the file operation under the target OS identity.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-POL-0001 — Your permission rules blocked this action
  • SMTO-POL-0003 — This command's folder is outside the allowed area
  • SMTO-FIL-0055 — SMTO can't save there because the drive is read-only
